review_standard: Mechanism labels require explicit wording, a detailed incident description, or reviewable injury footage with adequate visibility from a reputable source. A report of a challenge, collision, tackle, or ACL diagnosis alone is not treated as proof of direct or indirect contact. Earlier contact is classified as indirect only when it remains mechanically linked to the apparent injury action; contact followed by restored independent movement does not automatically convert a later unsupported action into indirect contact. Footage-based labels are marked as supported interpretations rather than explicit source labels, and uncertainty is retained when the injured knee or injury timing is obscured.

methodology.title: Systematic video analysis of ACL injuries in professional Spanish male football (soccer): injury mechanisms, situational patterns, biomechanics and neurocognitive errors
methodology.publisher: BMJ Open Sport & Exercise Medicine / PubMed Central

definitions.non_contact: No external contact is mechanically linked to the injury frame. Earlier contact followed by restored independent movement does not by itself disqualify a later action from this category.
definitions.indirect_contact: External contact or force not directly to the injured knee remains mechanically linked to the injury action.
definitions.direct_contact: External force was applied directly to the injured knee.
definitions.unclear: The available source does not resolve whether contact occurred or where it was applied. This includes contact-unspecified reports.
